summary: Dedicated (TP enabled): intermittent request timeouts / stalled streams under sustained load (8x GPU TP=8)
description:
Customer reports intermittent request timeouts and occasionally hung streaming responses on their Dedicated cluster when Tensor Parallel (TP=8) is enabled under sustained load.

Issue summary
- Symptom: ~0.5–2% of requests (higher during peaks) hit gateway timeout (504) or stall mid-stream until client timeout.
- Pattern: occurs under high concurrency + mixed sequence lengths (short chat + long context summarization) with streaming enabled.
- Customer note: disabling TP (switching to smaller model) eliminates the issue; using TP=4 reduces but does not eliminate.

Impact
- Customer experiences elevated error rate during business hours; internal dashboards show spikes in p95/p99 and timeouts.
- Customer has a production launch gate tied to Dedicated stability; requested workaround + timeline.

Environment (as provided)
- Dedicated cluster: nbx-ded-03 (eu-west)
- GPU: 8x NVIDIA H100 (SXM) per node (customer indicates 2 nodes in pool, autoscale disabled)
- Runtime version: 1.18.3-redwood (customer pinned)
- Model config: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, TP=8, streaming enabled
- Client: Redwood Python SDK 0.9.2 (async streaming)
- Traffic: 120–220 concurrent streams, prompt length mix (1k–20k tokens), max_tokens=512–2048

Steps to reproduce (customer’s approximation)
1) Run sustained traffic (>=150 concurrent streaming requests) for 20–40 minutes.
2) Include a mix of long contexts (>=16k) and short chats (<=2k).
3) Observe occasional requests hang mid-stream (no tokens), followed by gateway/client timeout.

What we observed / preliminary hypothesis
- Signature is consistent with a TP group entering a stalled state (no forward progress on one or more ranks), potentially due to:
  - collectives not surfacing async errors promptly, OR
  - cancellation / barrier interaction under streaming disconnects, OR
  - scheduler continuing to place work on a degraded TP group.
- This matches ongoing internal work on “TP stability fixes” (TP group watchdog + quarantine, improved cancellation semantics, improved async error checks).

Artifacts / logs (redacted)
- Gateway timeout sample:
  - 2025-02-10T18:42:11Z api-gw request_id=rgw_7d2f… status=504 route=/v1/chat.completions latency_ms=600000 model=llama-3.1-70b tp=8 customer=northbridge
- Runtime worker logs (rank-level excerpt):
  - [rank=3 tp_group=tp-19] INFO collective=all_reduce bytes=8388608 stream=comm0 started
  - [rank=3 tp_group=tp-19] WARN progress_stalled step=decode token_idx=47 elapsed_ms=90500 last_kernel="flash_attn" last_collective="all_reduce"
  - [rank=3 tp_group=tp-19] INFO request_cancel request_id=rt_91c… reason="client_disconnect" stage="streaming"
  - [rank=3 tp_group=tp-19] WARN barrier_wait barrier="tp_decode_step" elapsed_ms=120000
  - (no subsequent progress logs for tp_group=tp-19 until process restart)
- NCCL line seen intermittently (not always):
  - NCCL WARN Async operation still running on communicator 0x… (no fatal surfaced)

Customer request
- Immediate mitigation to reduce timeouts without large throughput degradation.
- Confirm whether this is a known issue and whether a hotfix is available for 1.18.x or requires 1.19.

Current workaround guidance (proposed)
- Reduce concurrency cap per TP group and avoid mixing extremely long contexts in the same pool (separate routing if possible).
- Increase gateway timeout only if acceptable (does not address stalls, only masks symptoms).
- If available in their build, enable conservative collective timeouts + fail-fast behavior so the scheduler can recycle bad TP groups instead of hanging indefinitely.

Next actions
- Support: coordinate log bundle + exact runtime build hash + cluster topology; confirm if hung requests correlate to streaming disconnect/cancel.
- Eng/SRE: compare hang signature to TP deadlock/cancellation issue; advise on safe flags and/or provide hotfix build.
- Customer: apply temporary load-shedding and re-test; report whether error rate drops.

resolution: Applied mitigations (LB idle timeout, concurrency cap) and rolled out runtime 1.19.1-hotfix with cancellation/barrier fixes + async error checks + TP-group watchdog/quarantine. Eliminated multi-minute stalls and reduced customer-visible timeouts to zero in the observed window.
next_steps: If watchdog quarantine events exceed agreed threshold, tune watchdog sensitivity via new config knobs (see pr-18473) with Runtime/SRE guidance.
Track overall TP stability initiative progress under ENG-2401; ensure Dedicated default-on plan is communicated via PM-512/PM-513.
Add customer-facing note to Dedicated runbook on LB/proxy idle timeouts for streaming endpoints.
